1	# Neutral default rails with environment profiles
 2	
 3	Replace DEFAULT_RAILS' author-specific content with a portable, generic deny/warn set (destructive git operations, pattern kills, home-directory deletion, agent-instruction file edits) that contains no absolute user paths, hostnames or ports. Move the OmniRoute-specific rails (warn-real-omp-config, warn-live-db, no-checkout-main's Desktop/OmniRoute path) into a shipped example profile under profiles/, loadable via config. Introduce path-token interpolation (${HOME}, ${planRoot}, ${cwd}) so rails can express machine-relative intent portably.
 4	
 5	## Rationale
 6	This is the single hardest adoption blocker. Five of seven default rails reference the author's machine; one silently fails to protect anyone else's repo because it hardcodes a Desktop/OmniRoute path. Without this, every other feature is invisible to every other user.
 7	
 8	## User Stories
 9	- [object Object]
10	- [object Object]

12	## Acceptance Criteria
13	- [ ] A grep for '/Users/nick', 'OmniRoute', '.omp', '20128', '20219', '20239' and 'launchctl' across src/ and shipped config returns zero matches
14	- [ ] DEFAULT_RAILS protects against git stash, git checkout/switch outside a worktree, pkill -f/killall, rm -rf on any home directory, and edits to CLAUDE/AGENTS/GEMINI.md using patterns that contain no absolute user paths
15	- [ ] Rail match strings support ${HOME}, ${planRoot} and ${cwd} interpolation, resolved at config load and unit-tested for each token
16	- [ ] profiles/omniroute.json reproduces the previous author-specific rail behaviour and is loadable via config.profile or --profile
17	- [ ] Existing tests in verdict-rails.test.ts pass unmodified against the neutral rail set, with added cases proving the checkout rail now fires for an arbitrary repo path
18	- [ ] Loading an unknown profile name fails config validation with a named error listing available profiles
